direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale very much feels like a plane-dad WWII movie with its look and feel because it genuinely feels like a fake movie at points, like if we had The Imitation Game or Oppenheimer at home; The direction on a microscale is fine overall, though at some points it does feel very over-the-top; The storytelling is good and builds the stakes well by using the severity of D-Day to amplify the movie, along with a side plot about the main character's wife potentially being bombed while giving birth; The tension of these stakes definitely helps set the scene and keeps you invested in the story

performance.comments: The definitive lead of the movie and definitely has a good presence on screen; while his character can feel a little subdued at times, he carries himself well and knows when to elevate his performance (especially in the more tense scenes); his chemistry is pretty good overall, especially with Condon and Fraser

A little too over the top as Eisenhower, especially in moments where he tries to hit higher octaves and higher notes when he's screaming, which feels kind of funny, campy, and over the top; overall he is fine, and has pretty good chemistry with Andrew Scott, Kerry Condon, and the rest of cast

My favorite performance in the movie as she really does let her presence be known when she's on screen; her Irish accent feels a little American at times, but she is good and needs to be constantly employed; her chemistry with Fraser and Scott is good and helps act as a good liaison and bridge between the two leaders

cast.comments: The cast as a whole feels very typical for a world war 2 movie and especially typical for a campy dad plane movie because it does add to this feeling like a fake movie; despite their over-the-top flaws, the cast as a whole has pretty good chemistry and helps elevate the main cast (who has good chemistry)

story.comments: The concept is pretty good, focusing behind the scenes on a historical World War II moment rather than taking you to the battlefield; The plot structure is fine overall for a retelling of history, though it drags a little bit toward the end where they could have cut about five minutes, but the climax is executed well and definitely helps the movie; The character writing is good, especially for the three main characters, as you get a clear angle on who they are as people and what their motives are; The character writing about the relationship between Eisenhower and Summersby is good because it helps allude to their potentially romantic affair, something that has been disputed in history

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is fine overall, though it definitely feels a little over-the-top at many moments; The dialogue very much matches the time period and gives it an old-timey feel; The humor is very old-timey but decent; The symbolism is not super deep because it is a historical movie that is very much just retelling and recounting moments in history; The foreshadowing is decent and definitely helps foreshadow what happens on D-Day

score.comments: It very much feels like a Volker Bertelmann score because it feels like a lighter version of All Quiet on the Western Front; It helps set the tone of the scenes and is used well to establish tension and raise the stakes

soundtrack.comments: The soundtrack is very minimal but helps set the time period for the movie

cinematography.comments: The cinematography is pretty basic overall, especially for a war movie, but it gets the job done; It kind of helps make this movie feel like a generic dad movie

editing.comments: The editing is pretty basic overall, but it gets the job done; It kind of helps make this movie feel like a generic dad movie

sound.comments: The sound is on the better side for a WWII movie, as it helps establish the war moments, but this movie is more about the war rooms rather than the war itself

visual_effects.comments: The movie is less about the war and more about planning, so when they do montages, it definitely feels like Oppenheimer at home; The D-Day and war moments are fine, but they definitely feel very generic and help add to the feeling of this being a generic, fake dad movie

production_design.comments: The production design was good and very much helped transport you to 1944 as they were planning D-Day and the invasion itself

makeup.comments: Used only really for Brendan Fraser, it helps make him look a little bit more like Eisenhower

costumes.comments: The costumes were good and helped transport you to the time period of World War II

review.pacing: The pacing is fine as it is, since the movie already has a pretty short runtime of an hour and 40 minutes; Some scenes drag a little bit toward the end where they could have cut maybe five minutes, but overall, it doesn't feel like they needed to cut much out
review.climax: The climax is executed well, though I was not a huge fan when it started because it felt like there was already a natural ending point where they could have just ended the movie; However, once the climax actually gets going, it definitely helps the movie a bit
review.tone: The tone is very much that of a World War II historical fiction movie, but instead of taking you to the battlefield, it takes you to the behind-the-scenes moments in the war rooms; It feels very much like having The Imitation Game or Oppenheimer at home; The movie very much feels like a fake movie with its generic dad-movie look, but it is not as bad as the promotional material makes it look
review.overall: Overall, while "Pressure" genuinely looks like a fake WWII dad movie that you would watch on a plane, it is definitely entertaining due to how they tell this real-life story, as the performances, especially from Andrew Scott and Kerry Condon, help build the stakes for this operation and keep you invested in whether or not D-Day goes as planned
